Check and Guard the Sequences of for Loops

Source: R/for_loop_nb_check.R
for_loop_nb_check.Rd

Checks the sequence of every for loop of a function. If the number of iterations is not fixed by the writing itself (e.g., 1:length(x)), a checking line is added before the loop, which warns at execution if the sequence is empty, contains NA or infinite values, has a single value, has only negative values, or starts decreasing (first value greater than the second). Prints the reported loops and returns a corrected version of the function.

Usage

for_loop_nb_check(
  x,
  export = FALSE,
  out_path = NULL,
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

Function to check, written without quotes and brackets (e.g., fun1 or pkg::fun1).

export

Single logical value. If TRUE, the corrected function is written into the <name>_safer.R file of out_path instead of being returned (e.g., fun1_safer.R for x = fun1 or x = pkg::fun1), as fun1_safer <- function(...), which base::source() recreates. Nothing is written if nothing has to be corrected, but an error is returned if the file already exists, or if x is not a function name (e.g., function(x){x} or FUN_LIST$fun).

out_path

Single character string: path of an existing folder where the file is written. Required when export is TRUE; otherwise not used, but a non-NULL value must still be a single non-empty character string. NULL by default.

safer_check

Single logical value. If TRUE (default), checks before running that the required packages and functions are installed and that the classical R operators (like <-) are not masked by another package or by a user-defined object of the global environment. These checks take time at each call: set FALSE in loops and inside other safer-r functions, to avoid repeating them.

lib_path

Vector of character strings: paths of existing extra library folders containing the required packages (e.g., packages installed without admin rights). They are searched after the current .libPaths() during the call (the current libraries keep priority), and .libPaths() is restored on exit. If NULL (default), only the current .libPaths() are used.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages (e.g., " INSIDE pkg1::fun1()") to name the calling functions. NULL is converted into "".

Value

The corrected function, which keeps the environment of x, or NULL, invisibly, if nothing has to be corrected or if export is TRUE.

A message is also printed: a table with one row per reported loop (column 1: line number; column 2: construct; column 3: code of the line) followed by the loops left unchanged, or a sentence saying that everything seems clean.

Details

Not reported: hard numbers, i.e., an integer-valued number, possibly negative, or two such numbers joined by : (e.g., 3, 1:3, 1e3, 1L:3L, 0:0, -3:-1, 1:0), whose iterations are fixed by the writing and left to the control of the writer, and a single seq_len(...) or seq_along(...) call, which gives no iteration for a zero length or an empty object.

Reported: everything else, e.g., for(i in x), 1:n, 1:length(x), 1:nrow(df), 1:(n - 1), seq_along(x) - 1, 1:2.5, 1:NA or 1:Inf. Comments, strings and the loops inside formulas, quote(), bquote(), expression(), alist() and substitute(), whose code R does not evaluate as written (e.g., quote(for(i in 1:n) x)), are ignored, except in the parts that R evaluates: .() in bquote() (..() too if splice = TRUE is written), and the where and splice arguments of bquote() and env of substitute().

Why: with x <- character(), for(i in 1:length(x)) runs twice, because 1:length(x) is c(1, 0). Use base::seq_along(along.with = x) instead.

Correction: each reported loop becomes tempo_for_seqN <- <SEQUENCE> ; <CHECKS> ; for(i in tempo_for_seqN)<BODY>, N being the rank of the report and <SEQUENCE> the sequence as written in the code, on a single line. The checks of negative and decreasing values only concern numeric sequences (not factors, dates, characters or complex numbers). Errors of the sequence itself (like 1:NA) are not caught. If the loop is not a standalone statement (e.g., unbraced body of an if, or argument value), it is enclosed in curly brackets. The rest of the code, comments and indentation included, is unchanged.

Warning: a reported loop is left unchanged, and listed in the message, when the name tempo_for_seqN is already used in the code (comments and strings included), when its sequence contains another reported loop, or when its sequence cannot be written on a single line with the same meaning (e.g., a sequence written on several lines that contains a comment, a string written on several lines, or statements on separate lines).

Warning: only the writing is analyzed. In n <- length(x) ; for(i in 1:n), 1:n is reported, whatever the value of n.

Source references: line 1 is the line of the function keyword. Comments and indentation are kept only if x carries its source references (attribute srcref). Functions created with options(keep.source = FALSE) (default of Rscript) and functions of installed packages (e.g., saferDev::colons_check) have none: their deparsed code is analyzed, without comments and with line numbers that differ from the source file.

See also

The code checkers of saferDev, in the recommended order of use: super_assign_check, lambda_check, colons_check, all_args_here, curly_bracket_check, true_false_check, for_loop_nb_check (see vignette("saferDev")).

Examples

# Without source references ("Run examples" link, Rscript), line numbers and comments differ.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/for_loop_nb_check.html
fun1 <- function(x){ for(i in base::seq_along(along.with = x)){ base::print(x = i) } }
saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(x = fun1, export = FALSE, out_path = NULL, safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL, error_text = "") # nothing to correct: NULL returned, invisibly
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::for_loop_nb_check().
#> INSIDE fun1(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
fun2 <- function(x){ for(i in 1:length(x)){ base::print(x = i) } }
fun2_safer <- saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(x = fun2, export = FALSE, out_path = NULL,
    safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "") # 1:length(x) reported
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME for() SEQUENCES ARE NOT WRITTEN WITH HARD NUMBERS:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 3	for		for (i in 1:length(x)) {
#> 
fun2_safer(x = base::character(length = 0)) # 1:length(x) is c(1, 0): the added checking line warns
#> Warning: FOR SEQUENCE STARTING DECREASING
#> [1] 1
#> [1] 0
# Write the corrected function in the fun2_safer.R file of a new temporary folder:
tempo_dir <- base::tempfile(pattern = "dir", tmpdir = base::tempdir(check = FALSE), fileext = "")
base::dir.create(path = tempo_dir, showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = FALSE, mode = "0777")
saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(x = fun2, export = TRUE, out_path = tempo_dir, safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME for() SEQUENCES ARE NOT WRITTEN WITH HARD NUMBERS:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 3	for		for (i in 1:length(x)) {
#> 
#> MODIFIED CODE EXPORTED IN:
#> /tmp/RtmpQNRq2A/dir11041c765204/fun2_safer.R
#> 
base::unlink(x = tempo_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = FALSE, expand = TRUE) # folder removed
